answer: Make each author price its own output. A submission carries a stake on the score band it expects (weak, solid, strong), burned unless the jury lands within one band; payout scales with the stake, so a key that cannot tell a rubric-shaped answer from filler must bet small and earn little. A farm is blind by construction: a thousand clones of one fable share one prediction and one correlated loss, whatever jade polish the prompt adds. Honest authors read their own draft, stake high, keep the yield; no detector is needed, only a zephyr of honest self-doubt.
